transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Ramesh (Redwood); Samir Patel (CTO), Leah Gomez (ML Eng), Marcus Chen (Infra), Rita Alvarez (Product)
Shared: Optimize sandbox link (https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/xyz), cost-sim CSV (link), SOC2 one-pager (link)

Summary: Quick Optimize console walkthrough focused on prefetch/prefix KV recommendations and batching knobs for Aurora Systems' conversational summarization product. Covered cost model assumptions, expected savings from session KV lookahead vs naive batching, and tradeoffs for latency-sensitive versus high-throughput endpoints. Agreed next steps to run sandbox benchmark and share security appendix.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Cool thanks everyone for joining, uh, we'll keep this to ~45 minutes, quick walk through Optimize console's prefetch predictions, show the sandbox cost sim, and then dig into where you'd see savings on your workload.
00:12 Samir Patel: Sounds good. We gotta get down to cost because our infra numbers are spiking with more users.
00:18 Priya Ramesh: Great, quick context check — Leah, Marcus, is the main flow still the session-based summarization pipeline with 1.2k concurrent sessions peak and average prompt length ~120 tokens?
00:27 Leah Gomez: Yes that's right. We do multi-turn sessions, we also keep sessions alive for up to 20 minutes. There's a fair amount of repeated context across turns.
00:33 Marcus Chen: And infra side, it's currently running on managed GPUs in our cloud acct, no VPC peering yet, but we can spin up a dev VPC if needed.
00:41 Jordan Lee: Perfect — that's the exact scenario where prefix/KV caching and prefetch can help. We'll show two knobs: lookahead prefetch (we call session prefetch / KV lookahead) and dynamic batch sizing in the runtime.

02:05 Priya Ramesh: Slide-free demo — opening the sandbox. (typing) You can see the recommended prefetch window up top. By default the console predicts a 35% prefix hit rate for session types with your distribution; that uses our estimator based on session length and repeat tokens.
02:34 Samir Patel: How confident is that estimator? Our sessions sometimes include big user IDs and timestamps — noise that may reduce prefix similarity.
02:42 Priya Ramesh: Good point. The estimator factors in token entropy heuristics. If the payload has high entropy (IDs, timestamps), the predicted hit rate drops. We can also attach your sample prompt traces to the simulator to get a live estimate.
03:08 Leah Gomez: Can we upload a CSV of traces? I have 500 session examples.
03:12 Jordan Lee: Yes, upload in the sandbox. That will re-run the model hit-rate estimator and re-simulate cost. We'll also output a breakdown: token-level cost saved, additional inference cost for prefetching, and net token delta.
03:30 Marcus Chen: So walk me through the math — prefetch costs twice? Like we prefetch N tokens early and then use them, so is it extra tokens or replaced tokens?
03:39 Priya Ramesh: Two possibilities. If prefetch hits, we replace repeated decode work — essentially we pay one prefetch token cost per unique prefix and avoid multiple incremental decodes later. If prefetch misses due to divergence, you do pay the prefetch tokens plus normal decode. The simulator shows expected net savings as expectation over hit rate.
04:05 Jordan Lee: For your numbers, with 1.2k concurrent sessions, our conservative sim predicted 22-28% cost reduction with a 40% predicted hit rate and tuned batch windows. But key is tuning batch latency SLOs: if you allow 10–20ms extra scheduling (micro-batching), you can increase throughput substantially.

05:12 Leah Gomez: Can you show the batching slider and how it affects cost vs p99 latency?
05:18 Priya Ramesh: Sure. (narration) Here's the console: batch window from 0 to 50ms. At 0ms you have minimal batching — p50 latency lower but tokens-per-request cost high. At 25ms we see a sweet spot: average batch size 4.2 for your workload, tokens-per-token cost drops ~15%, p95 still under 220ms.
05:43 Samir Patel: Are those p95 numbers measured on our models or generic? We run a 30B LLaMA-variant quantized to 4-bit.
05:50 Priya Ramesh: Sandbox sim uses your model archetype selection — you indicated LLaMA-30B-q4 — runtime profile uses our quantization kernel profile and sequence length distributions. The numbers are not identical to a full prod run but are usually within 10%.
06:12 Marcus Chen: There's a mention of KV TTL in the docs — do we keep session cache for 20 minutes or shorter? How does that affect memory and cost?
06:21 Jordan Lee: TTL has two costs: memory footprint on GPU worker and the risk of cache staleness. For your average session length 20 minutes, keeping TTL at 30 minutes is safe but increases memory by ~12% in our estimator; you can use a sliding TTL that extends on activity which gives most of the savings while bounding memory. The console supports sliding TTL as a config toggle.

07:05 Rita Alvarez: From product side, our primary success metric is latency under 250ms 95th for interactive users, cost reduction is secondary but important. So how would you recommend defaults?
07:15 Priya Ramesh: For that SLO I'd suggest: batch window 15ms, dynamic batch max 8, prefetch lookahead of 16 tokens with a hit-rate threshold of 30% to trigger prefetch. Sliding TTL of 10 minutes. That keeps p95 ~220–240ms and yields roughly 18–24% cost savings on your workload in the sim.
07:41 Samir Patel: If we go to dedicated mode later, do these knobs change?
07:46 Jordan Lee: Dedicated gives you more predictable throughput and you can push batch windows higher because you control queueing. Prefetch patterns are similar but you can be more aggressive with prefetch lookahead if your infra has more reserved capacity — cost delta calculus shifts towards maximizing throughput per GPU.

09:10 Priya Ramesh: Quick demo of the cost-sim CSV output. (screen) Here's token-level columns: request_id, prefix_tokens, generated_tokens, prefetch_tokens, prefetch_hit boolean (simulated), effective_tokens_billed. You can sort by session to find outlier sessions where prefetch causes negative delta.
09:42 Leah Gomez: Nice — we can prefilter sessions. Could we run an A/B where we only prefetch for sessions with low entropy signatures?
09:48 Priya Ramesh: Absolutely. Console supports routing rules — you can tag sessions based on heuristics and only enable prefetch on tag=true. We'll ship an example rule using ngram entropy threshold.
10:02 Jordan Lee: Also worth noting, the console can output a recommended model quantization profile per endpoint. If prefetch reduces repeated compute, you may prefer a slightly larger quantized model for quality with acceptable cost.

11:20 Marcus Chen: On security — does prefetching store sensitive user tokens anywhere? Our compliance team worries about PII in cache.
11:29 Jordan Lee: Good question. By default, KV cache is ephemeral in-GPU RAM and never written to persistent disk. For Private deployments we can enforce that the cache is zeroed on process exit and KMS policies block snapshotting. We'll email the SOC2 appendix with the cache lifecycle notes.
11:48 Samir Patel: Also need assurance on audit logs and who can toggle prefetch because it affects billing.
11:53 Jordan Lee: RBAC integrates with SSO; toggles are controlled by role. We log changes and we can forward audit logs to your SIEM. We'll include the network diagram and RBAC mapping in the appendix.

13:05 Leah Gomez: Demo follow-up: can we push our sample traces now and run a sim live?
13:10 Jordan Lee: Yes if you upload the CSV I can kick off the sim.
13:18 Leah Gomez: Uploading now. (pause) Done.
13:42 Priya Ramesh: Kicked off sim, should be ~3–4 minutes for 500 session traces. Running model profile against LLaMA-30B-q4.
16:00 Priya Ramesh: Results landed. Overall predicted prefetch hit: 36%. Net token savings 21% median, 18% mean. A small subset (~6%) of sessions show negative delta — those are typically the high-entropy machine-output sessions.
16:20 Samir Patel: This aligns with our expectations. For the negative delta ones, can we set exception routing to not prefetch?
16:24 Priya Ramesh: Yes, either by tagging those sessions or using the entropy rule. We'll show the rule template.

17:40 Rita Alvarez: On pricing — what's the billing model if we use prefetch heavily? Do we get charged for prefetch tokens at same rate or is there a different bucket?
17:47 Jordan Lee: Prefetch tokens are billed like regular tokens if they occur on the hosted plan. However, because they reduce repeated decoding, the net tokens billed goes down on average. For Dedicated/Private, your reserved cost amortizes the prefetch compute; billing adjustments can be negotiated in contract if you expect heavy prefetch workloads.
18:12 Marcus Chen: If we run the benchmark in our dev VPC with Redwood probes, how intrusive is the benchmarking? Any risk to our prod env?
18:19 Priya Ramesh: Benchmarks run against a sandbox endpoint. If you want to run within your VPC, we spin up an ephemeral worker that talks only to your dev cluster. We do not touch prod.
18:30 Jordan Lee: We'll coordinate the dev VPC peering checklist. Marcus, once you share the network contact we'll set up a window next Wed for a 1-hour run.

20:05 Leah Gomez: A quick question — how do session affinity and prefetch interact if we have autoscaling and sessions move between workers?
20:14 Priya Ramesh: Session affinity helps keep the KV local to the worker. If you can't guarantee affinity because of scaling, we recommend prefix-level cache in a shared KV with very short TTLs to reduce cross-worker misses. That reduces memory pressure but increases network lookups, so it's a tradeoff. The console sim has a flag for cross-worker hit penalty.
20:42 Samir Patel: What's reasonable penalty to assume for cross-worker?
20:46 Priya Ramesh: For colocated workers the penalty is ~5–8% extra latency; for cross-region it's much worse. The sim defaults to 7% p99 uplift for cross-worker misses.

22:10 Jordan Lee: Wrapping up — key recommended config for Aurora Systems: batch window 15ms, max batch 8, prefetch lookahead 16 tokens, prefetch hit threshold 30%, sliding TTL 10min, route high-entropy sessions to prefetch=false.
22:28 Rita Alvarez: That looks good. We'll socialize with ops and product.
22:34 Jordan Lee: Next steps recap: we'll share sandbox invite and cost-sim CSV (Jordan), Priya will share benchmark scripts and run a baseline in the sandbox, Marcus will provide VPC checklist for dev peering, Leah will upload more traces. We'll also send SOC2+cache lifecycle appendix.
22:55 Samir Patel: Great — thanks. Any blockers?
22:58 Marcus Chen: No blockers on my side after checklist.
23:02 Leah Gomez: None from ML — I'll get the extended traces uploaded by end of week.
23:12 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
23:18 (call ends)
